newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Benchmarking to boost EU competitiveness.
newsitem.headline: Benchmarking to boost EU competitiveness.

text.p: European Union industry ministers urged the European Commission on Thursday to put forward proposals for developing the use of so called benchmarking as a tool to boost the competitiveness of European industry.

In conclusions adopted at the Industry Council, ministers said benchmarking was beneficial in improving the environment for industry through "monitoring competitiveness in its diverse aspects and must be directed ultimately towards meeting the needs of enterprises, including SMEs."
The conclusions responded to the Commission's communication on October 9 on benchmarking the competitiveness of Europe's industry, which is lagging behind both the United States and Japan.
Benchmarking involves constant comparisons of industry practices in different areas with the best performers in the world, giving examples on how to improve.
It is a practice which is spreading and industry has welcomed the Commission's report.

The Council's conclusions said the competitiveness of the EU vis-a-vis its major trading partners "needs to be kept continuously under review, in order to identify areas where improvement is needed and policies and strategies require to be adjusted."
The agreed text said the Commission could act as a "facilitator" for member states in the use of benchmarking.
It called on member states and the Commission to identify areas where further benchmarking could be needed and how it should be carried out as well as to initiate pilot projects.
